Ramil Khafizov

I’m a PhD researcher at the Applied AI Institute, working on generative models, visual foundation models, and 3D computer vision. My research explores how generative models can use geometry to synthesize consistent views and reconstruct the 3D world.

I work on next-scale autoregressive generation, geometry-aware attention, and adapting visual foundation models with camera and depth priors. Previously, I was a deep learning researcher at Artec 3D, where I worked on generative 3D editing, spatial vision-language modeling, and promptable 3D segmentation.

Email/ CV/ Google Scholar/ GitHub

Research

I’m interested in efficient generative modeling and the intersection of appearance and geometry: autoregressive models, diffusion and flow matching, novel-view synthesis, and feed-forward 3D reconstruction.

NAMVIS: Next-Scale Autoregressive Multi-View Image Synthesis

Ramil Khafizov, Ilya Statsenko, Ruslan Rakhimov, Artem Komarichev, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

NeurIPS, 2026

project page / paper / code / bibtex

G-CUT3R: Guided 3D Reconstruction with Camera and Depth Prior Integration

Ramil Khafizov, Artem Komarichev, Ruslan Rakhimov, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

arXiv preprint, 2025

paper / code / bibtex

Feed-forward 3D reconstruction that incorporates available depth, camera calibration, and pose priors through modality-specific encoders and zero-initialized fusion.
